title: Marketplace listing compatibility heuristics and snippet rotation
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft that pulls together: a) pragmatic compatibility heuristics we can use to decide whether a given Redwood product configuration is marketplace-ready; b) a compact checklist for the engineering and legal gates required for a publishable tile; and c) a lightweight plan for snippet rotation and copy variations for AB tests and fallbacks.

Audience:
- GTM PMs and content writers preparing listing copy
- Partner/ISV owners integrating Redwood Dedicated/Private flows
- Eng owners (product infra, private-deployments, dedicated) responsible for preflight checks

Scope / constraints:
- Focused on cloud marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP) seller tiles and one-click connectors.
- Includes variants for Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on-prem) product configurations.
- Not a full legal checklist; high-level flags only.

Quick summary (one-liner):
- Make it clear which deployment mode the listing supports (hosted | dedicated | private). Use explicit banners and a SKU table.
- Provide a tiny compatibility matrix (network/KMS/region/entitlement) so buyers know if their org can onboard without a support ticket.
- Rotate 3–4 hero + description snippets during the first 2 weeks of listing to surface best conversion language, and keep a fallback snippet set for rollback.

Compatibility heuristics (accept/reject quick checks):
1) Deployment mode compatibility
   - Hosted API: Accept if public API keys can be provisioned automatically and quota limits are mappable to marketplace metering.
   - Dedicated: Accept if we can map reserved capacity SKUs to marketplace billing and guarantee minimum throughput SLA in the region.
   - Private: Accept only if customer-managed network/KMS instructions are documented and there’s an onboarding playbook.

2) Data residency and region mapping
   - Must list supported cloud regions for the tile and highlight any region-level differences (e.g., eu-west1 does not yet have dedicated pools).
   - If model weights or logs cannot leave region X, add explicit note in the listing and docs.

3) Telemetry & tracing requirements
   - Listing must declare what telemetry is shared with Redwood (metrics, error rates) and how long logs are retained for tile customers. If a marketplace requires specific telemetry hooks, call them out.

4) Security/KMS/Credential flow
   - If tile needs KMS/HSM: include step-by-step and an example CloudFormation/ARM/Terraform snippet for the credential wiring.
   - If tile uses proxying or token exchange, include diagram link.

5) Trial entitlement and provisioning
   - Must define: trial duration, quota (tokens or inference units), and auto-cleanup behavior.
   - If provisioning requires manual activation (support ticket), mark listing as "assisted trial" and call that out in the tile copy.

6) Fallback/compatibility mapping (key operational pattern)
   - If preferred model (quantized open variant) unavailable in region, runtime should fall back to compatible variant and we must document expected latency/cost delta in the listing.
   - Provide an explicit fallback matrix: preferred model -> backup model -> degraded feature set.

Listing copy checklist (visual + copy assets):
- Tile name (short, unique): one-liner, no trademark conflicts.
- Hero blurb (10–14 words): quick value prop for engineering buyers.
- 3 supporting bullets (feature + outcome): latency SLA, cost predictability, private/VPC capability.
- 2 screenshots: Console onboarding screen + telemetry dashboard. Include captions (what you’ll see).
- 1 short demo GIF (15–25s) of provisioning.
- Icons & logo in required sizes (SVG and 1x/2x PNG).
- Terms snippet for pricing: per-token + optional reserved capacity SKU mapping.

Suggested hero blurb variants (rotate these):
A) "High-throughput LLM inference with enterprise controls — predictable latency at scale."
B) "Ship LLM features faster: low-latency inference, private deployments, and cost controls."
C) "Redwood: unified serving across hosted, dedicated and private environments."
D) "Enterprise inferencing that scales — reserve GPU pools or use our hosted API."

Description bullets (short):
- "Dedicated pools & autoscale: reserve capacity for consistent latency under load."
- "Network-isolated private deployments: VPC connections and KMS integration for regulated data."
- "Batching, caching, and quantization recommendations to cut token costs up to 5x."

CTA variants (order these for rotation):
- Primary: "Start free trial" (hosted)
- Primary: "Request reserved capacity" (dedicated)
- Secondary: "Contact sales for on-prem" (private)

Snippet rotation plan (first 30 days):
- Day 0–3: Hero A + Bullets canonical. Monitor CTR and conversion.
- Day 4–10: Rotate Hero B and D (each for 3 days) while keeping bullets constant.
- Day 11–20: Test CTA variants and reorder bullets (lead with private vs lead with cost).
- Day 21–30: If conversion delta < 8% across variants, settle on best-performing snippet and move remaining variants into a 3-month secondary rotation.
- Always keep a minimal fallback hero and CTA for quick rollback.

Acceptance criteria before submit to marketplace portal (preflight):
- All assets present and validated (icons, screenshots named correctly).
- Billing SKU mapping documented and test invoice flow validated in staging.
- Trial provisioning flow verified end-to-end (automated or clearly documented manual step).
- Security review passed for KMS/keys flow and no IP leaks in screenshots.
- One-page quickstart doc uploaded and linked in tile.
- At least one e2e smoke test: provision tile -> call API -> verify billing event. Add to CI if possible.

Smoke test checklist (minimal):
- Provision tile in test account (automated script).
- Generate an API key or entitlement.
- Run identity+network check (VPC reachability or proof-of-ownership flow).
- Send sample inference request; assert healthy status and response time under SLO for sample load.
- Confirm billing record appears with correct SKU mapping.

Post-launch monitoring & rollback guardrails:
- Monitor first 72 hours for: failed provisions, entitlement mismatches, unexpected billing spikes.
- If >5% of provision attempts fail in first 24 hours, pause listing and flip to assisted-purchase flow.
- Keep a pre-approved fallback copy set and a technical rollback checklist (tile unpublish -> revert listing -> notify partners).

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- How granular should the public compatibility matrix be? (region-by-region vs per-continent) @Arjun
- Need legal to sign off on the trial terms snippet (sla/credits behavior). @Lina
- Should we include an "on-prem quickstart" as a downloadable PDF or keep it behind request?

Links & references (working):
- Confluence onboarding runbook: CONFLUENCE-78910
- Billing mapping PR: github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-tiles/pull/88
- Marketplace onboarding Slack thread: slack:#marketplace-onboarding (thread ts: 1723456789.000200)
- Example infra snippet for GCP KMS binding: [private snippet in repo]

Quick notes to self (copywriter):
- Keep technical jargon limited in hero — buyer is an engineer but tile listing must scan quickly.
- Emphasize predictable unit economics. Avoid absolute numbers unless region-certified.
- Use "private/VPC" phrasing consistently across hero and bullets.

Immediate next steps (action items):
- Arjun: drop sample CloudFormation and a 1-click Terraform snippet into the repo (JIRA-4521). Due: 2024-11-15.
- Lina: loop legal on trial terms + write the short T&Cs paragraph. Due: 2024-11-18.
- Ben: prepare two screenshots and one GIF from the staging console. Due: 2024-11-12.
- Maya: assemble final asset zip and draft portal submission copy. Due: 2024-11-20.

Notes on tone and risk:
- Tone: concise, engineering-focused, slightly opinionated on economics (we win on predictable cost + deployment flexibility).
- Risk: Overpromising latency across regions. Always specify region differences and expected deltas.

If this looks good I'll:
- convert to the marketplace portal JSON template (I have a skeleton under github PR linked above),
- create a staging submission and request a 48-hour smoke window with marketplace ops,
- schedule a 30-min dry-run with Partner Ops to walk through assisted-trial flows.

Unresolved: where to surface the fallback model matrix (tile UI vs docs). Leaning to both: short line in tile, full matrix in quickstart doc.

End of draft.

-- Maya
